patch.value: The overrun guard asserted a recovery outcome it never checked and reported update failures with no item id

Review round 3 on PR 59 found two remaining gaps in the buffer overrun work, both of the same family as the defect the PR exists to remove: a message that states something the code did not establish. First, when a create overran its receipt and the recovered orphan was closed as a recovery step, the close result was discarded while the thrown error claimed the orphan was closed. If that recovery close itself failed or was killed, the operator was told the orphan was handled and stopped looking for an item that is still open. Second, a pm update or the terminal pm close in the update path could persist its mutation and then return a null status or a non-zero exit, and the resulting error named neither the item nor the possibility that the write had landed, so the row was reported as a generic failure with nothing to reconcile against. The fix inspects the recovery close result and words the error for its actual outcome, and makes every update and terminal close failure carry the item id together with an explicit statement that the mutation may already have been applied. The guarantee is stated in the code as no mutation is left un-identified, which is narrower and more honest than no mutation is left behind. See the linked feature for the capability that would be needed to widen it.

The recovery close result is inspected and the thrown error distinguishes an orphan that was closed from one that is still open, carrying the close's own failure cause; the recovery close is attempted exactly once rather than retried, because under a capped buffer it fails identically every time; every pm update and terminal pm close failure in the update path carries the item id and states that the mutation may already have been applied; each new error arm has a regression test and every test is mutation-tested by reverting its fix and confirming it fails; coverage thresholds are unchanged and measured coverage does not regress

value.author: claude
value.text:
Acceptance evidence for review round 3 on PR 59.

Finding A (Greptile P1, upsertCreate recovery close). The recovery close result is now captured
and inspected. On status 0 the error states the orphaned item was closed; on a null status or a
non-zero exit it states the orphan is STILL OPEN, must be closed manually, and carries the close's
own cause (describePmNullStatus for a null status, the close stderr otherwise). The close is
attempted exactly once: under a capped buffer it fails identically every time, so a retry loop
would only turn a fast actionable error into a slow one. The docstring now states the guarantee
and its limit: the extension cannot make pm create atomic (a single subprocess with no transaction
the caller can join), so a window always exists where the item is persisted and the caller does not
yet know it; what is guaranteed is that the window is always reported WITH THE ID.

Finding B (Greptile P1, upsertUpdate). Every pm update and terminal pm close failure now carries
the item id and states explicitly that the mutation may already have been applied. The null-status
arm and the non-zero arm are handled separately, because a non-zero exit is not proof that nothing
was written. When the terminal close fails after a successful update, the message reports BOTH: the
update WAS applied and the close may have been too. Update compensation was deliberately NOT added
(see pm-csv-71zg): an update has no inverse without the prior field values, so compensating it
could only mean writing some other value over it, which is a second unreviewed mutation rather than
a rollback. The docstring states the narrower guarantee in those words: no mutation is left
UN-IDENTIFIED, not no mutation is left behind.

Gates, all green and run after the final restore:
- typecheck: clean.
- build and build:test: clean.
- Full suite: 127 tests pass (123 after Finding A's tests, plus 4 new update-path tests).
- coverage: index.ts 84.18 lines / 80.26 branches / 88.66 funcs, UP from round 2's
  83.62 / 78.42 / 88.66. Thresholds 81 / 74 / 88 UNCHANGED. No c8 ignore added.
- audit:prod: 0 vulnerabilities.
- pack:dry-run: 9 files, 64.1 kB.
- changelog:check: up to date.

Mutation testing of the four new update-path tests. Reverting the upsertUpdate fix to the previous
assertPmOutputFit plus generic-message form makes exactly 4 of the 28 tests in atomic.test.ts fail,
and restoring it returns 28 of 28 passing. The four are the only tests asserting the new messages,
so all four are load-bearing. Finding A's three tests were mutation-tested in the same way when
they were written.

Test infrastructure added: two tracker-scoped fake pm markers, fake-update-fail (exit 1 with a
simulated stderr) and fake-update-kill (SIGKILL, producing status null), alongside the existing
fake-close-fail and fake-close-kill. Each marker only acts when present in the tracker root under
test, so concurrent test files are unaffected while PATH is temporarily mutated.

Provenance note: the production code for both findings was written by a pi agent (glm-5.2) whose
provider hit a usage cap before it could run the gates, create the items, or commit. The four
update-path regression tests, the mutation testing, every gate run, and this record were completed
by the orchestrator, which also verified the agent's code rather than accepting it. One unrelated
edit the agent left behind, a deletion of two extension merge-driver lines from .gitattributes, was
reverted as out of scope.

patch.value: Both review round 3 findings fixed on PR 59. The recovery close in upsertCreate is now inspected rather than assumed, so the thrown error distinguishes an orphan that was closed from one that is still open and carries the close's own failure cause; it is attempted exactly once because under a capped buffer it fails identically every time. Every pm update and terminal pm close failure in the update path now carries the item id and states explicitly that the mutation may already have been applied, with the null-status and non-zero arms handled separately because a non-zero exit is not proof nothing was written. Update compensation was deliberately not added and is tracked as pm-csv-71zg: an update has no inverse without prior field values, so compensating it would be a second unreviewed mutation rather than a rollback. Gates green: typecheck clean, 127 tests pass, coverage 84.18 / 80.26 / 88.66 up from 83.62 / 78.42 / 88.66 with thresholds 81 / 74 / 88 unchanged, audit 0 vulnerabilities, pack 9 files, changelog up to date. The four new update-path tests are mutation-tested: reverting the fix fails exactly those four of 28 and restoring it passes all 28.
